newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania hopes for better terms for new bond.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania hopes for better terms for new bond.

text.p: The Baltic state of Lithuania said on Friday it was confident the coupon on its planned $200 million eurobond issue would be lower than that paid on its two previous issues.
The finance ministry earlier announced it was inviting proposals from 15 international banks to arrange a $200 million bond issue. A decision on which bank is expected in March.
"We expect to get a better coupon and better terms for this issue," Ruta Skyriene, the deputy director of the finance ministry's international department, told Reuters.
"Our previous international bonds were issued before we got our credit ratings," she added.
Lithuania made its debut on the international capital markets in December 1995.
It launched a two-year, $60 million eurobond led by Nomura with a coupon of 10 percent. A $50 million bond under similar conditions followed in mid-1996.

Lithuania was the first former Soviet republic to obtain a credit rating last September when Moody's assigned it investment grade ratings of Ba2 for its foreign currency debt and Ba3 for its bank deposits.
"The new bond will be used for overall budget needs such as financing the deficit and servicing the debt," Skyriene added.
Lithuania's budget deficit in 1997 is planned at 697 million litas and the country's parliament set a borrowing limit of $618 million.
